name: Paygent Connect
website: docs.nmi.com (NMI gateway; official Paygent site not confirmed)
verdict: No OAuth app review exists: each merchant needs a live gateway account and a portal admin who creates a key and pastes it in. Whether Paygent uses NMI is unconfirmed, so get the real docs first (low confidence).
needGuide: No — collect each merchant's private key, but first confirm what Paygent Connect's API actually is.

auth.detail: No official 'Paygent Connect' developer site could be found; paygent.com redirected to a domain-for-sale page. Assuming it is built on the NMI gateway (per the task hint, unconfirmed), NMI uses security keys: public keys for client-side use and private keys for server-side, created in Settings → Security Keys of the Merchant Portal (or Partner Portal). v5 endpoints take the key in the Authorization header; Classic APIs take an api_key body field. Keys inherit the permissions of the associated user. OAuth appears only for NMI's partner Merchant Sign-Up API (access token expires after 60 minutes).

effort.timeToFirstTest: 30–60 min with a sandbox or test-mode account
effort.timeToProduction: unknown (depends on merchant account approval; likely days to weeks)

approval.gate: Each merchant needs a live gateway account (underwriting by the processor or reseller, likely) and must hand your app a key. Becoming an NMI partner (Partner Portal, Partner Code onboarding, Merchant Sign-Up API) is separate and optional. No user-facing OAuth app review exists.

scopes.why: Key permission types chosen when the key is created.
scopes.summary: Key permission types chosen when creating the key (list not documented in the pages read); public keys for client-side tokenization, private keys for server-side. Grant the minimum needed (for example query-only for reporting).

cost: Gateway fees are charged to the merchant; developer fees unknown
prerequisites: Account and owner: A company-owned gateway or partner account with permission to create security keys; separate keys per app and environment.
Where you register: Merchant Portal → Settings → Security Keys → Add a New Key → name, associated username, key permission → Create. Partners: same path in the Partner Portal.
Cost: Gateway fees are charged to the merchant; developer fees unknown

registerAt.path: Merchant Portal → Settings → Security Keys → Add a New Key → name, associated username, key permission → Create. Partners: same path in the Partner Portal.

steps.do: Confirm with the vendor that Paygent Connect is NMI-based and obtain the real developer docs
Merchant admin creates a key: Merchant Portal → Settings → Security Keys → Add a New Key
Build a credentials form that accepts the private key, stored encrypted, one key per merchant and environment
Validate with a Query API call or a test-mode transaction
Test with sandbox keys and test cards, including declines and webhooks
Add key rotation and revocation instructions (create new, update, test, revoke old)

roles.team: A company-owned gateway or partner account with permission to create security keys; separate keys per app and environment.
roles.console: Keys are tied to portal users, so add a dedicated user with least-privilege permission; no collaborator roles documented beyond that.
roles.customer: The merchant's portal administrator creates a key, assigns minimal permissions and pastes it into your app. Under a partner account, a key can also be created through the Create Merchant API Keys endpoint.

testing: NMI documents a sandbox/test mode, Testing Methods and test cards, and a Gateway Emulator; the homepage links a full-featured sandbox.
Verify that your gateway reseller enables test mode.

blockers.fix: No official Paygent Connect docs were found; confirm the vendor and gateway before building.
Use least-privilege user permissions and never expose them client-side.

blockers.problem: Keys inherit the creating user's rights
blockers.fix: If that user is disabled the key may stop working (likely).

blockers.problem: Sandbox may need enabling by the reseller

automation.agentCan: Write the credentials form, validation call and transaction code against the NMI API; draft customer instructions for creating a key.
automation.humanMust: Merchant account application and underwriting, portal login to create keys, any partner agreement, and identifying the correct vendor contact.

uncertain: Whether Paygent Connect actually uses NMI or has its own API; the official Paygent site and docs; permission types; partner requirements; fees.
The NMI docs do not mention Paygent.
